title: Eddie Design System — full catalog
description: Every component, recipe, chart and page template in the Eddie graph, as A2UI v1.0-shaped catalog nodes. Reference document; products should consume a profile.
instructions: Subset of the upstream default catalog used by the resources hydration compiler. Original schemas and metadata retained.

Stack.description: A block-axis rhythm owner: lays its children out in a single column with a consistent, token-driven gap between them.

gap.description: Gap The space between children, as a spacing role (preferred) or t-shirt size. Pick the role by what the children *are* to each other (docs/SPACING.md): - `block` (default) — cards, features, modules: the blocks inside a region.

children.description: The siblings to space. Every direct child becomes a column item separated by the gap.

eddie_useWhen: several sibling blocks are stacked vertically and need the same space between them
a set of media blocks, article cards or feature rows should run down the page, a single item per row, instead of being boxed into a grid of cards
loose blocks inside a card, a sidebar or a panel have nothing around them that owns the space between them
eddie_notWhen: the items should sit side by side and wrap — use `ed-cluster`
the children are the paragraphs, headings and lists of a piece of writing — use `ed-text-passage`, which owns the rhythm of prose
the items should form columns — use `ed-grid`, or `ed-layout` for a main column with a narrower one beside it
the things being spaced are the titled regions of a page — use `ed-main`, which already spaces the `ed-section`s inside it

the items are short, mostly-text rows that read as a list — a feed, a set of search results — use `ed-list`, so assistive technology hears a list; richer items (media blocks, article cards, features) are stacked here
a lone sentence or button would sit among whole regions — compose it inside the `ed-section` it belongs to; one gap cannot suit both

Section.description: Start a new segment of a page with a title and an optional one-line description — the most common structural move on any content page.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of the section header (heading and description). Never affects the body slot (#1496) — body content inherits the page's alignment and opts into centering on its own terms.

flush.description: Flush Cancels the rhythm the section body owns between its children (docs/SPACING.md), for bodies whose content manages its own edges (e.g. a single full-bleed visual). Fine-tuning without going flush: set `--ed-section-gap` on the host.

children.description: The main section content (body)

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

header.description: Section heading and description (typically ed-heading and ed-text-passage components)

eddie_useWhen: a region of a page needs a title — a heading, and perhaps a short introductory sentence — above the content
a long page should read as a sequence of labelled parts
a reader scanning a long page needs signposts telling them what every part covers

the title and its one-line description should sit centred over the content of a landing or marketing region — that is the default `align="center"`, and it is the reason to stop writing `text-align` CSS around a loose heading (#1492)
a heading and a one-line passage have been written as consecutive siblings directly above a block of content — that lockup is this component's `header` slot
eddie_notWhen: the region needs a coloured or full-bleed background — use `ed-band`, with the section inside it if it also needs a title

the content is one item in a set rather than a region of the page — use the display that fits the set: `ed-card` for browsed visual peers, `ed-media-block` for a person or a comment, `ed-r-article-card` for a post (docs/CHOOSING-A-DISPLAY.md)
the block is a marketing moment with a large image, a headline and a call to action — use `ed-feature`
there is no title to give it — omit it and let `ed-main` or `ed-stack` space the content
the title is the title of the whole page — use `ed-page-header`
only a title is needed, with no body beneath it to group — use `ed-heading`
the shift is a change of subject inside one region, too slight to deserve a title — use `ed-hr`

Heading.description: Semantic heading component that renders the appropriate HTML heading tag (`h1`–`h6`) with flexible typography styling via preset variants.

variant.description: Typography variant that controls visual style independently of heading level. If not set, defaults based on `tagName`: h1→headline-lg, h2→headline-default, h3→headline-sm, h4→title-lg, h5→title-default, h6→title-sm.

tagName.description: The semantic HTML heading tag (h1–h6). Decoupled from visual style to allow correct document structure regardless of visual hierarchy. Defaults to h2.

wrap.description: How the heading breaks across lines. Leave it unset — headings balance (`text-wrap: balance`, which is also what `"balance"` names explicitly) by default, which evens the line lengths out and is what a title wants nearly always.

visuallyHidden.description: Remove the heading from view while leaving it in the accessibility tree and the document outline.

enhance.description: Enhance mode: progressive enhancement of author-written light-DOM markup; see AGENTS.md. Author the real elements yourself; not for generated specs, whose children are catalog nodes. Supported since 0.50.0

children.description: The heading text content. Slot an `<a>` here to make the whole heading a link — it is styled by the system, so don't add your own link CSS

eddie_useWhen: screen-reader users navigating by headings should be able to find this part of the page
a title has to look bigger or smaller than the outline level implies
a title should also link to the item it introduces
a short eyebrow line should sit above a title — and it genuinely labels what follows, since it adds an entry to the outline
eddie_notWhen: it is the title of the whole page together with a description — use `ed-page-header`
it is the headline of an opening banner — use `ed-hero`, and slot this component into it as the `h1`
the words should merely look large or bold and are not a title of anything — use `ed-text-passage`
the titles sit inside CMS or markdown prose — use `ed-text-passage`, which styles the headings inside it
a region needs a title and a description above content — use `ed-section`, and slot this component into it

TextPassage.description: Container for rich text content from CMS or markdown sources.

knockout.description: Knockout color variant for dark backgrounds. Adjusts text and link color for proper contrast on dark surfaces.

inverted.description: @deprecated Use `knockout` instead. `inverted` is a backward-compatible alias scheduled for removal on 2026-10-12 (3 months after its 2026-07-12 deprecation). See issue #1020.

size.description: Size variant that scales the overall typography up or down from the default body size.

capLinelength.description: Constrain maximum line length to an optimal reading width. When enabled, wraps content in an `ed-linelength-container` to prevent uncomfortable long lines. Disable for full-width layouts or when width is pre-constrained.

children.description: The text passage content — unclassed HTML as a CMS or markdown renderer emits it: `p`, `h1`–`h6`, `ul`/`ol` (nested too), `dl`/`dt`/`dd`, `blockquote`, `figure`/`figcaption`, `table`, `hr`, `img`, `iframe`, `pre`/`code`, and inline `kbd`, `…

eddie_useWhen: the body of an article, a post or a product description arrives as markdown or HTML from a CMS and needs to look right without a class on any element
comments, reviews or forum posts contain whatever formatting their authors chose, and nobody controls the markup
long-form writing needs comfortable spacing between paragraphs, headings and lists
eddie_notWhen: the words are a lone title — use `ed-heading`
the content is being assembled from Eddie components rather than arriving as raw HTML — compose it directly, with `ed-stack` for the spacing
a stray sentence would sit by itself between regions of a page — compose it inside the `ed-section` it introduces, or the `ed-page-header`
the text is a snippet of source or a terminal command — use `ed-code`
the prose only needs a narrower measure — use `ed-linelength-container` around it, or this component's own line-length cap
the words are being collected from a visitor rather than displayed — use `ed-textarea-field`

Text.description: A run of text inside a container: plain text, or wrapped in a p / span / strong / em / li. Use it for paragraphs in a TextPassage, the value inside a StatCard, a label inside a Button.

tagName.description: Optional wrapper element; omit for a bare text node.

Grid.description: A responsive CSS Grid container for laying out child `<ed-grid-item>` elements. Supports multiple responsive column variants (2up, 3up, 4up, etc.), gap sizing (none, sm, lg), and breakpoint control (faster, slower).

variant.description: Column layout variant. **Pick by how narrow an item can get before it stops working, not by how many items you have.** The variant sets the column count at each width, so the question it answers is "how much room does one of these need?" A…

gap.description: Gutter between grid items. Unset is the default gutter, which suits cards and anything else carrying its own border or surface. - `"none"` — Items meet edge to edge.

break.description: Shifts where the chosen `variant` changes column count. It never changes the counts themselves — if you want different counts, pick a different variant. - `"faster"` — Break to more columns at narrower widths.

children.description: The grid items (typically `<ed-grid-item>` components)

eddie_useWhen: a collection of like items — cards, thumbnails, tiles, entries — should sit in equal columns that collapse to one on small screens
the items are peers: any one of them could swap places with another without changing what the page means
a listing or catalog of visual items — projects, courses, merchandise — needs laying out
a short set of recommended or related videos — lessons that answer a question, "watch next" — is chosen from by looking
a dashboard needs a row of stat or summary cards of equal importance
wordless miniatures — the logos of clients or partner organisations, avatars, swatches — need tidy equal columns
eddie_notWhen: one or two items in the set deserve more visual weight than the rest — use `ed-r-bento`, whose cells span different widths and heights
the columns are unequal, or one is chrome around another (content + sidebar) — use `ed-layout`
the items are one row that should wrap at their own natural widths (tags, chips, a row of buttons) — use `ed-cluster`
there is one column of siblings — use `ed-stack`, whose gap is a spacing role
the items are label-and-value facts about a single subject — use `ed-key-value-table`
order in time is the point — use `ed-timeline`
every item is a small picture beside a few lines of text, such as a person or a comment — use `ed-media-block`s in an `ed-stack`
there are only a few items and every item carries a large picture, a headline and an action — use `ed-feature`, read in turn down the page
most visitors want only a couple of the entries, as in an FAQ — use `ed-accordion`
the items are short labels such as topics or filters — use `ed-tag-list`
the items are text only and there are many of them — use `ed-list`; a column per title multiplies the length of the page
people will compare the items across the same attributes (dates, prices, places) — use `ed-table`, which puts each attribute in a line the eye can run down
there is a single item, or the job is capping the measure — use `ed-layout-container`
items must overlap or be positioned freely — no Eddie layout does that; compose it inside the component that owns the overlap

GridItem.description: A child element of `<ed-grid>` that represents a single grid cell. Grid items automatically adapt to the responsive column layout defined by their parent grid's `variant` prop.

children.description: The content of the grid item (cards, images, text, etc.)

eddie_useWhen: wrapping each piece of content that should occupy one cell of an `ed-grid` — every child of a grid needs one
a card, thumbnail, or tile needs to stretch to its cell so a row of them lines up
eddie_notWhen: the cell should span several columns or rows — `ed-grid` has equal cells only; use `ed-r-bento-item` inside an `ed-r-bento`
there is no `ed-grid` parent — the cell gets no layout at all; use `ed-layout-container` or the content on its own
you are tempted to nest one inside another — put one `ed-grid-item` per cell directly under `ed-grid`

Card.description: A flexible container component that organizes content into three distinct zones: a visual media region, a core content body, and an actions region.

variant.description: Style variants. Unset is the default outlined card: surface fill, subtle border, and shadow. - **outlined** The default look, named.

padding.description: Inset between the card's edge and its content — body, header media, and footer actions alike. Unset is the medium inset.

align.description: Align variants - **center** renders a card that has center aligned content/text

children.description: The card's core content: headings (`<ed-heading>`), body copy (`<ed-text-passage>`), and any other primary descriptive elements. This is the default slot — most of what you put in a card goes here, including the card's title/heading

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

header.description: Media/visual slot: images, icons, illustrations, or other visual content above the body.

footer.description: Actions on **what the card is about** — open it, buy it, read it. Buttons, button groups or other interactive controls only; not metadata or footer text, which belong in the default slot.

actions.description: Actions on **the card itself** — rename, delete, duplicate, pin. Sits in the block-start inline-end corner (top-right in LTR), inset to line up with the body, and overlays `header` media when there is any.

eddie_useWhen: a set of browsable items — products, courses, projects — share the same parts: a picture, a title, a line or so of description and perhaps an action
several unrelated things share a screen and the eye needs telling where an item ends and the next begins
a panel in a dashboard needs a surface to hold a chart, a table or a summary
eddie_notWhen: the items are label-and-value facts about a single subject — use `ed-key-value-table`
every item has the same attributes and readers compare across them — use `ed-table`
order in time is the point — use `ed-timeline`
the items are mostly text and there are many — use `ed-list`, `ed-link-list` when every row is only a link, or `ed-r-article-card` for dated entries with an excerpt
the item is a small picture beside a few lines of text, such as a person or a comment — use `ed-media-block`
the items are numbers — use `ed-r-stat-card`
a few items deserve more weight than the rest — use `ed-r-bento`
there are only a few items and every item carries a large picture, a headline and an action — use `ed-feature`
most visitors want only a couple of the entries, as in an FAQ — use `ed-accordion`; for a few parallel views shown in turn, `ed-tabs`
the items are short labels such as topics or filters — use `ed-tag-list`
the content is a region of the page rather than an object in it — use `ed-section`

VideoCard.description: A card for one video people pick from — a course lesson, a talk, a demo: a 16:9 thumbnail with a play glyph, a linked title, a one-line meta, and an optional excerpt clipped to three lines, composed on a bare `ed-card`.

text.description: The video's title, rendered as the card's heading. Use the title verbatim. Named `text` rather than `title` on purpose: `title` is a global HTML attribute and would give the whole card a browser tooltip.

href.description: Where the video lives. The title links here, and so does the thumbnail (for pointer users only). Without it the title is plain text and the thumbnail isn't a link.

imgSrc.description: The thumbnail image. Without it the card draws the placeholder: a quiet 16:9 surface with the play glyph centered.

imgAlt.description: Alternative text for the thumbnail. Defaults to empty, because the title already names the video.

meta.description: One line of context under the title: "AI & Design Systems · Chapter 5 · TJ Pitre". Nouns joined by a middle dot, not a sentence.

duration.description: The video's length as a clock ("12:34", "1:02:05"), drawn on the thumbnail. Screen readers hear it in words in the meta line.

headingTagName.description: Semantic heading tag for the title (h2–h6). Defaults to `h3`, which assumes the set sits inside an `h2`-titled section. Pick by the outline, never for size: one level below the heading that introduces the set.

variant.description: The card's look, forwarded to `ed-card` (#2019). Unset renders the flush `plain` card this recipe is built around: the thumbnail and the text align with their neighbors in a grid, and the thumbnail carries the visual weight.

padding.description: The card's inset, forwarded to `ed-card`. Unset is flush (`none`). Give it an inset when you also give it a surface (`outlined`, `subtle`, `strong`): `sm` for an ordinary card, `lg` for a featured one that stands alone.

children.description: (default) The excerpt: a sentence or two about what the video covers. It's clipped to three lines; the full text stays in the DOM.

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

media.description: Replaces the thumbnail. Leave it unslotted and pass `imgSrc` (or nothing, for the placeholder).

title.description: The video title. Leave it unslotted and pass `text` + `href`; slot an `ed-heading` containing a plain `<a>` when the title needs markup the prop can't carry.

meta.description: One short line of context: course, chapter, who's in it. Leave it unslotted and pass `meta`. Keep it to one line — it's the card's single use of the Meta register.

eddie_useWhen: someone needs to choose one video from a handful — the lessons that answer their question, what to watch next, a talk from an archive
videos have no thumbnails yet but should still look like videos
eddie_notWhen: the reader should watch without leaving the page — use `ed-r-video-embed`
nothing in the set is a video — use `ed-r-article-card`, or `ed-r-project-card` for a still image
people will scan dozens of results by their titles — use `ed-list`
the set is a history read in date order — use `ed-r-timeline-node-video`

Timeline.description: A timeline that displays a chronological sequence of entries along a shared connecting line. Wraps `ed-timeline-node` children — bare, content-agnostic containers — to give them the line, correctly-sized markers, and consistent spacing.

orientation.description: Layout axis: `vertical` (default) runs the connecting line top-to-bottom; `horizontal` runs it left-to-right with nodes laid out as columns.

arrangement.description: Node arrangement: `stacked` (default) places every node on the same side of the connecting line; `alternating` flanks the line so consecutive nodes appear on opposite sides.

behavior.description: @deprecated Renamed to `arrangement` (#1249) — this alias maps to the same values and is removed in the release after next. When both are set, `arrangement` wins. See `arrangement` for what `stacked` and `alternating` do.

size.description: Default marker size for every child node: `sm` (1.5rem) · `md` (3.25rem, default) · `lg` (4rem) · `xl` (5rem).

markerBorder.description: Draw a border on every child node's marker. The switch: it turns the ring on at the `md` width in the default border color; `markerBorderWidth` and `markerBorderColor` refine it.

markerBorderWidth.description: Marker border width for every child node: `sm` · `md` (what the `markerBorder` switch uses) · `lg` · `xl`, from the `--ed-theme-border-width-*` scale — plus `none`, which is only useful as a per-node opt-out.

markerBorderColor.description: Marker border color for every child node, each value a `--ed-theme-color-border-*` token. Setting a color implies the border. - `default` — the neutral rule color, and what the bare `markerBorder` switch uses.

markerShadow.description: Box shadow on every child node's marker: `sm` · `md` · `bold` (the stacked offset shadow, `bfw` only and falling back to `md` in the other themes) — plus `none`, useful as a per-node opt-out.

layout.description: Layout mode: unset (default) renders the single connecting line; `snake` (#1371) wraps the timeline into serpentine runs with true half-circle U-turns.

runLength.description: Nodes per snake run (a row by default; a column with `orientation="horizontal"`). Unset, runs auto-fit the container inline size and re-wrap on resize, like text. Only meaningful with `layout="snake"`.

motion.description: Built-in motion treatment (#1375, the animate axis from #1249 — named `motion` because a property named `animate` would shadow the native `Element.animate()` method).

scrollable.description: Give a horizontal timeline its own horizontal scroll container (#1423). Without it, horizontal orientations compress every node into the container width — 24 entries become 24 unreadable slivers.

curve.description: Draw the connecting line as one smooth spline through the node anchors instead of straight runs (#1372).

reveal.description: How much of each entry's content is showing at rest (#1426): - `always` (default) — every entry's content is visible; the timeline reads as a list.

labelReveal.description: How much of each entry's marker LABEL is showing at rest (#1455) — the `reveal` axis applied to the bead rather than the body: - `always` (default) — the label sits in the dot, as it always has.

children.description: Timeline node elements (`ed-timeline-node`)

eddie_useWhen: a career history, the phases of a project or the releases of a product should unfold chronologically
the gaps and the busy stretches between dated entries are part of the story
a personal site wants to present years of posts, talks and releases as a single continuous stream
eddie_notWhen: the entries have dates but are browsed in any order, like a blog index — use `ed-list` or `ed-r-article-card`
somebody needs to find a particular release and check who shipped it — use `ed-table`
there is a single entry — use `ed-card`
the items have no order — pick the display from docs/CHOOSING-A-DISPLAY.md: `ed-list` for text, `ed-table` for compared attributes, `ed-grid` with `ed-card` for browsed visual peers

TimelineNode.description: A bare, content-agnostic entry container on a timeline: a circular marker on the parent's connecting line plus a content slot.

variant.description: Color of the default marker dot, using `ed-dot`'s token-backed vocabulary. Unset renders the brand background color. Leave it unset for a line whose entries are all one kind.

size.description: Per-node marker size override: `sm` (1.5rem) · `md` (3.25rem) · `lg` (4rem) · `xl` (5rem). Unset inherits the parent timeline's `size`. Leave it unset and size the whole line on `ed-timeline`.

label.description: Short text rendered inside the default marker dot — a type ("video", "book") or a stacked date (a newline in the value renders as a line break, e.g. `nov\n2026`). Centered on both axes, colored with the variant's on-color token.

current.description: Marks this node as the present-moment / featured entry ("you are here"): a ring emphasis orthogonal to `size`, reflected to `aria-current="true"`.

markerBorder.description: Draw a border on this node's marker. The switch: it turns the ring on at the `md` width in the default border color, and `markerBorderWidth` / `markerBorderColor` refine it.

markerBorderWidth.description: Marker border width: `sm` · `md` (what the `markerBorder` switch uses) · `lg` · `xl`, from the `--ed-theme-border-width-*` scale — plus `none`, which removes a border this node inherited from its parent timeline.

markerBorderColor.description: Marker border color for this node, each value a `--ed-theme-color-border-*` token. Setting a color implies the border, and overrides whatever the parent timeline cascaded.

markerShadow.description: Box shadow on this node's marker: `sm` · `md` · `bold` (the stacked offset shadow; `bfw` only, falling back to `md` in other themes) — plus `none`, which removes a shadow inherited from the parent timeline.

href.description: Permalink for this entry. When set, the marker renders as a plain `<a>` — always pair with `hrefLabel` for an accessible name.

hrefLabel.description: Accessible name for the marker link (its `aria-label`). Required whenever `href` is set — the marker has no visible text of its own.

reveal.description: How much of this entry's content shows at rest (#1426): `always` (default), `hover` (fades in when the entry is hovered or focused), or `tooltip` (lifts out of flow into a bubble under the marker).

labelReveal.description: How much of this entry's marker LABEL shows at rest (#1455): `always` (default), `hover` (fades in inside the dot when the entry is hovered or focused), or `tooltip` (lifts out of the dot into a bubble).

children.description: The entry's content (heading, date, body, media — typically a timeline node recipe or composed Eddie atoms)

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

marker.description: Custom marker replacing the default dot, clipped to a circle (`ed-dot`, image, iframe, visualization) — or a lone `ed-icon`, which rides the dot instead of replacing it

eddie_useWhen: an entry in a career history, a changelog or the phases of a project holds something no ready-made entry covers, and its content will be composed by hand
a single entry in a chronology should stand out from its neighbours — larger, marked as the present moment, or carrying cover art in its marker
eddie_notWhen: the entry is a blog post, a talk, a book, a video or another kind with a ready-made entry — use that `ed-r-timeline-node-*` recipe, such as `ed-r-timeline-node-blog`
markup written for the older attribute-driven entry needs to keep working — use `ed-r-timeline-node`
it is not on a timeline — use `ed-card`, or `ed-list-item` in an `ed-list`
a free-standing coloured circle in a diagram — use `ed-dot`

TextLink.description: Semantic link component with flexible typography and styling variants.

rel.description: The `rel` attribute for the rendered `<a>` — an unordered set of space-separated link-relationship tokens, passed through verbatim.

target.description: Where the link opens. Leave it unset for almost every link — the same tab is what people expect, and it keeps the Back button working.

variant.description: Visual variant controlling prominence and scale. - `display`: Large, prominent link. For the single link a block exists to offer — a featured item, the next article — when it is not a heading.

size.description: Size variant for reducing typography scale. - `sm`: Smaller than default If not set, uses default size.

knockout.description: Knockout color variant for dark backgrounds. Adjusts link color for proper contrast on dark surfaces.

inverted.description: @deprecated Use `knockout` instead. `inverted` is a backward-compatible alias scheduled for removal on 2026-10-12 (3 months after its 2026-07-12 deprecation). See issue #1020.

children.description: Link text content

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

linkAfter.description: Optional content appended after the link text (e.g., icon)

eddie_useWhen: a word or phrase inside a sentence should take the reader somewhere else
a small cross-reference such as See also or View source should sit quietly beside content
a block exists to present a single destination, such as the next article or a featured story, and that link should be large
eddie_notWhen: clicking does something rather than going somewhere — use `ed-button`
several links form a group, as in a footer column or a sidebar — use `ed-link-list`
the link is a title that belongs in the document outline — use `ed-heading` with a plain anchor slotted into it
the links are the site's navigation — use `ed-primary-nav` or `ed-utility-nav`
the link should look like a button — use `ed-button` with an href

TableObject.description: A responsive wrapper for `ed-table` that adds horizontal overflow scrolling with gradient edge indicators, plus optional header and footer regions.

behavior.description: Behavior variants - **overflow** gives every column heading a minimum width (7rem), so the table grows with its column count - **overflow-small** gives the whole table a minimum width (750px) Pick by what makes the table too wide.

children.description: The contained element, usually a table or `ed-table`

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

header.description: Content to appear above the table

footer.description: Content to appear below the table

eddie_useWhen: a table has more columns than a phone can show, and should scroll sideways rather than squash
a table needs a title, filters or a results count above it, or pagination and totals beneath it, kept together as one unit
eddie_notWhen: the table always fits and needs nothing around it — use `ed-table` alone
the rows are label-and-value facts about a single subject — use `ed-key-value-table`, which needs no sideways scrolling
something other than a table is too wide — omit it; the edge fades only respond to an `ed-table` inside
the bar above the table holds several controls — use `ed-toolbar` in the header region, and `ed-pagination` in the footer

Table.description: A semantic table component for displaying structured data in rows and columns. Tables support variants for visual styling (zebra striping, hover effects) and full-width layouts.

variant.description: Style variants * - **zebra** Alternating row colors to improve readability in dense data tables

hoverRows.description: Hover rows variant 1) If set to true, rows can be hovered over and change color to help readability

fullWidth.description: Full-width variant 1) Table expands to the full width of its container when set to `true`

label.description: Accessible label for the horizontal scroll region that wraps the table. When a wide table can't fit its container it scrolls within its own bounds (rather than overflowing the page — #1247).

children.description: The table structure (ed-table-header and ed-table-body)

eddie_useWhen: readers need to compare items across the same attributes — which features every pricing plan includes, workshops by dates, city and venue
somebody is looking up a particular record in a long set of transactions, orders or members
figures need lining up in columns so they can be read down as well as across
comparing suppliers or contracts by cost, reliability and renewal dates; the dates are record attributes rather than values being entered
eddie_notWhen: label-and-value facts about a single subject — use `ed-key-value-table`
the items are browsed by their pictures rather than compared — use `ed-grid` with `ed-card`
a few headline numbers — use `ed-r-stat-card`
rows of mostly text with no shared columns — use `ed-list`
arranging parts of a page — use `ed-grid` or `ed-layout`

the shape of the figures matters more than reading them exactly — use `ed-r-bar-chart` for categories, `ed-r-line-chart` for change over time; every chart carries its own data table, so the figures stay reachable
the table is wider than a phone, or needs a title bar and a footer around it — use `ed-table-object` around this component

TableHeader.description: Table header section container. Renders as semantic `<thead>` element. Contains a single `ed-table-row` with `ed-table-header-cell` children for column definitions.

children.description: Table header rows (typically one ed-table-row with header cells)

TableBody.description: Table body section container. Renders as semantic `<tbody>` element. Contains multiple `ed-table-row` children with `ed-table-cell` content for data rows.

children.description: Table body rows (multiple ed-table-row elements)

TableRow.description: Table row container. Renders as semantic `<tr>` element. Used in both `ed-table-header` (with header-cell children) and `ed-table-body` (with cell children).

children.description: Table cells (ed-table-cell or ed-table-header-cell elements)

TableHeaderCell.description: Table header cell. Renders as semantic `<th>` element with scope="col". Used in table-header rows to define column headers. Supports alignment, vertical alignment, column spanning, and sortable behavior.

colSpan.description: Column span prop 1) Used for spanning cells to a set number of columns

rowSpan.description: Number of rows this cell spans, rendered as the native `rowspan` — the twin of `colSpan`.

align.description: Align variants - **right** renders a table cell with horizontally right aligned content - **center** renders a table cell with horizontally center aligned content Match the cells beneath: **right** over a column of numbers or currency, **ce…

verticalAlign.description: Vertical align variant * - **center** Vertically aligns content to the middle of the cell

behavior.description: Behavior variant - **sortable** Makes the header cell interactive with a sort toggle, use for columns that support data sorting The cell only flips its own arrow and `aria-sort`; it fires no event and reorders nothing.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction - **ascending** renders a delta-up icon to represent ascending order of column cells - **descending** renders a delta-down icon to represent descending order of column cells - **none** the unsorted resting state — no icon, `a…

children.description: Header cell content (column title or custom content)

eddie_useWhen: a column of a table needs a name, so that every figure beneath it is announced with its heading
readers should be able to reorder the rows of a table by clicking a column's name
eddie_notWhen: it holds a value rather than the name of a column — use `ed-table-cell`
it would label a row of facts about a single subject — use `ed-key-value-table-row`, which renders the row heading itself
the heading is for the whole table rather than a column — use `ed-heading`, in the header region of an `ed-table-object` around the table

TableCell.description: Table data cell. Renders as semantic `<td>` element. Used in table-body rows to display cell content. Supports horizontal and vertical alignment, and column spanning.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of cell content - **right** Use for numeric or currency data that benefits from right alignment - **center** Use for centered content like status indicators or icons **right** for anything read by magnitude, so the digi…

verticalAlign.description: Vertical alignment of cell content * - **center** Vertically center content for alignment with icons or tall cells

colSpan.description: Column span prop 1) Used for spanning cells to a set number of columns

rowSpan.description: Number of rows this cell spans, rendered as the native `rowspan` — the twin of `colSpan`.

children.description: Cell content (text, components, or HTML)

eddie_useWhen: a row of a table needs one of its values placed under a column
a summary row should stretch a total or a no-results message across several columns
eddie_notWhen: it names a column rather than holding a value — use `ed-table-header-cell`
the row is a label and its value about a single subject — use `ed-key-value-table-row`
the value is a status in a word or two — put an `ed-tag` inside the cell rather than colouring the cell

Tabs.description: A tabbed interface component that organizes content into multiple panels. Only one tab is active at a time; clicking a tab label shows its content panel.

knockout.description: Knockout color variant for dark backgrounds. Adjusts the tabs' colors for proper contrast on dark surfaces.

inverted.description: @deprecated Use `knockout` instead. `inverted` is a backward-compatible alias scheduled for removal on 2026-10-12 (3 months after its 2026-07-12 deprecation). See issue #1020.

activeIndex.description: Active tab state 1) Sets the initial active tab (e.g. 0 sets the first tab, 1 sets the second tab, etc.)

align.description: Align variants Unset, the tabs start at the reading edge, which is right for most uses. - **center** aligns the tabs in the center of the screen on medium/large screens.

children.description: Tab panels (ed-tab elements)

slots.description: Named-slot children, keyed by slot. Each value is a child list.

tabsAfter.description: Optional content after tab list (filters, actions, etc.)

eddie_useWhen: account settings split into a few parallel areas such as profile, billing and notifications, a single area visible at a time
the same subject can be viewed several ways — overview, activity, files — and visitors switch between views
a code sample is available in several languages
eddie_notWhen: readers need to compare the content of the panels — use `ed-table`, or plain `ed-section`s so everything stays visible
there are many panels, or labels too long to fit in a row — use `ed-accordion`
the choices lead to different pages — use `ed-primary-nav` or `ed-link-list`
steps that must happen in order — compose `ed-section`s in sequence; tabs imply no order
a single block of optional detail — use `ed-show-hide`
the control turns a preference on or off rather than changing what is displayed — use `ed-toggle`
the choice is a value submitted with a form rather than a change of what is displayed — use `ed-radio-field`
the control moves between pages of the same results — use `ed-pagination`

Tab.description: Tab panel component for use within ed-tabs containers. Each tab represents a content panel with a label (shown in the tab list trigger) and content (shown when the tab is active).

ariaLabelledBy.description: Aria labelledby property 1) Used to connect tab trigger and tab panel for accessibility

href.description: An author-chosen id for the panel. Set it when the panel must be addressable by an id you control — a deep link, a test selector, a persisted "last open tab". Leave it unset otherwise: the panel generates its own unique id.

tabId.description: Tab ID 1) Used to connect the href of the tab trigger to the panel

label.description: The trigger text. The parent `ed-tabs` renders it as this panel's tab in the tablist, so it is the panel's accessible name too. Every tab needs one: 1–2 words, sentence case, parallel across siblings ("Overview", "Pricing", "Reviews").

children.description: Tab panel content (shown when tab is active)

BarChart.description: Bar chart recipe — categorical data rendered with Chart.js 4.

data.description: Chart data — labels and one or more datasets with optional semantic hints. A `null` in a dataset's `values` is a category with no data: no bar is drawn and the data table reads "no data". Use `0` only for a measured zero.

orientation.description: Bar orientation: `vertical` (default) or `horizontal`. `vertical` when the categories have a natural order along the bottom — months, quarters, age bands — and their names are short.

variant.description: Multi-series layout: side-by-side (`grouped`, default) or layered (`stacked`). `grouped` when readers compare the series with one another inside a category — this year against last.

chartLabel.description: Accessible label for the chart region (required for a11y). Write it as `chartLabel` or `chart-label`; both bind, like every multi-word Eddie prop.

dataTable.description: Render a toggle-able linked data table (default `true`). Write it as `dataTable` or `data-table`; both bind, like every multi-word Eddie prop.

children.description: Optional extended description (e.g., a trend callout) rendered between the chart and the data table.

eddie_useWhen: readers should see which of several categories leads, and by how much — teams, products, channels, answers to a survey
this year should sit beside last year for every category, or a total should show what it is made of
eddie_notWhen: a measure is followed through continuous time and the rise and fall is the story — use `ed-r-line-chart`
the point is how a whole divides into a few shares — use `ed-r-doughnut`
what happened must be told apart from what is expected — use `ed-r-projection`
reading the exact figures is the main job, or there are more than twenty or so categories — use `ed-table`; the chart's own data table is a fallback for assistive technology, not the display
there are only one or two headline numbers — use `ed-r-stat-card`

Tag.description: A compact labelled pill: a category, a status, a filter, a keyword.

behavior.description: What this tag does. `static` (the default) is an inert label. `link`, `action` and `selectable` expect you to slot the matching interactive element — this renders chrome around it and nothing else.

variant.description: Semantic colour. Unset renders the neutral default. - `brand`: brand-coloured — for a label that promotes rather than reports: New, Featured, Pro.

appearance.description: Emphasis, orthogonal to `variant`. - `subtle` (default): tinted background, coloured border and text - `solid`: filled knockout background, no border.

size.description: Typography and padding step. `sm` (default) or `md`. A tag is compact by definition; there is deliberately no `lg` or `xl`. `sm` sits inside dense content — table rows, card meta, a byline.

iconName.description: Optional leading icon, rendered before the label and inheriting the tag's content colour. Decorative — never the only carrier of meaning.

text.description: The label, as a property. **Prefer slotted content.** A string prop renders nothing until JavaScript runs, so a `text`-only tag is blank on first paint without Declarative Shadow DOM, while slotted text is there in the markup.

dismissed.description: Hidden after a dismissal. Settable to restore a tag you removed optimistically and then had to bring back.

children.description: The tag's content. Plain text for `static` and `dismissible`; your own `<a>` for `link`; your own `<button>` for `action` and `selectable`.

eddie_useWhen: an article, a product or a record needs a short label saying which category it belongs to or which state it is in
a row in a table needs a status such as Draft, Published or Failed at a glance
the filters applied to a listing should appear as chips that can be removed
visitors narrow a listing by toggling facets
eddie_notWhen: the control triggers an action such as Save or Delete — use `ed-button`
several labels appear together — use `ed-tag-list` around them
the message is a sentence, or demands attention — use `ed-alert`, or `ed-field-note` under a form field
the label is a key on the keyboard — use `ed-kbd`
a person should be identified — use `ed-avatar`

TagList.description: A semantic list container for arranging multiple tag elements with consistent spacing.

label.description: Accessible name for the list, rendered as `aria-label` on the inner `<ul>` — the element assistive technology reads.

children.description: Tag elements (`ed-tag` components) to arrange in a list

eddie_useWhen: an article, a product or a search result carries several keywords, topics or categories
shoppers should see at a glance which refinements are narrowing their results, and clear any of them
eddie_notWhen: only a lone label is needed, such as the status of a table row — use `ed-tag`
the row mixes labels with buttons, bylines or icons — use `ed-cluster`
the items are the navigation of the site rather than topics or keywords — use `ed-link-list`
the row holds Save, Cancel and the like — use `ed-button-group`

antiPatterns.reason: an anchor wrapping a button nests two interactive controls; assistive technology announces both and keyboard focus lands twice
antiPatterns.fix: give ed-button an href so it renders as the link itself

antiPatterns.reason: a link inside a button nests two interactive controls
antiPatterns.fix: use ed-button with href, or ed-text-link for an inline link

antiPatterns.reason: the header slot is for media only; a heading there paints as an image band and loses its place in the document outline
antiPatterns.fix: put headings and copy in the default slot, media in header, actions in footer

antiPatterns.reason: the header slot is for media only; prose there is styled as an image band
antiPatterns.fix: put ed-text-passage in the default slot

antiPatterns.reason: a grid only lays out ed-grid-item children; anything else is not a grid cell and stacks in a single column
antiPatterns.fix: wrap every card or tile in its own ed-grid-item

antiPatterns.reason: a grid item inside a grid item is a cell with no grid; the inner item is inert
antiPatterns.fix: put one ed-grid-item per cell directly under ed-grid

antiPatterns.reason: a hero already constrains its content to the measure; a layout container inside doubles the padding and breaks the full-bleed treatment
a hero manages its own internal layout and full-bleed background; capping it in a layout container clips both
antiPatterns.fix: place ed-hero directly inside ed-main and put ed-layout-container inside the sections that follow

antiPatterns.reason: nested layout containers cap the measure twice and double the inline padding
antiPatterns.fix: keep one ed-layout-container per region and let sections sit inside it

antiPatterns.reason: the recipe already renders the fieldset; nesting another puts a legend inside a legend
antiPatterns.fix: slot the ed-checkbox-field-items straight into ed-r-todo-list

antiPatterns.reason: the inline checkbox does not re-emit its change event, so the list can never count it
